comment: Template for $DAPILOT_STORE_DIR/reference/pricing-policy.json; scripts/dev/shop.sh setup copies it there when missing. The values are dapi's own shop as decided 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-11. Review seller_region, currency, vat.rate, vat.purchase_reclaimable, markup_pct and cost_basis for your shop before pricing anything. The hard rule, enforced by price_candidates.py --check and never by a prompt: the sale price is never below break-even (cost plus platform fees plus VAT owed).

vat.in_sale_price_note: Conservative: treats every sale as VAT-inclusive as for EU buyers. US buyers pay sales tax on top through Etsy, so for a US-heavy shop this understates net by up to 21%. Flip to false once the buyer mix is known.
vat.purchase_reclaimable_note: Our own shop buys from our own platform; no VAT leaks. An external EU seller without a VAT number sets this false.

hard_rules: price >= break_even, always, for any author of price.json
the model picks only from candidates; a price that is not a candidate needs a human override block
the model never writes an override block; only a person does
min_margin_note: Soft rule for the model only: candidates whose margin on net revenue is below this are listed under rejected and not proposed. A person may still pick one with an override block, as long as it is above break-even.
cost_basis_note: full_plate: the unit price at max_per_plate from the batch curve. Decided 2026-09-11: the shop buys in batches (about stock_units at a time) and sells from stock, so the plate price is the real unit cost. one_off is what print-to-order would cost and is reported beside it.
stock_units_note: Units bought per production run. Drives the stock block in viability.json: plates, batch cost, payback units per candidate. Not a cap on anything.
